title: Tech Note: Modular Interface Design Using Picture Variables
author: Forrest Swilling
featured_technology: PICT resources loaded via ACI Pack (GetPicture)
MacsBug (Macintosh low-level debugger, used for RAM measurement)
ResEdit and Customizer Plus (resource editing/Update resource for 4D Server clients)

historical_commentary.text: This note shows how to use non-enterable picture variables loaded from PICT resources (via ACI Pack) as shared, modular backdrops for fields and controls, demonstrating with 4D Insider/MacsBug measurements that this approach is far more file-size- and memory-efficient than duplicating 4D graphic objects or embedding large PICTs on every layout; the specific tooling (ResEdit-based PICT resources, ACI Pack, Customizer Plus's Update resource, MacsBug) is entirely classic Mac OS/4D v3.x-era, but the underlying UI-efficiency principle of reusing shared bitmap assets instead of duplicating graphics per-layout remains a recognizable, still-valid idea in modern UI design.
related_updates: ResEdit, MacsBug, PICT resources, and 4D Insider are all obsolete classic Mac OS/4D v3.x-era tools with no modern equivalents in current 4D or macOS
Modern 4D form/object architecture provides native picture/icon object types and modern image formats, removing the need for hand-loaded PICT resources and ACI Pack's GetPicture command
Customizer Plus and the .res/.rex client resource file model described here reflect a 4D Server client architecture that has been substantially modernized in later 4D versions
